title: Output planes for a 4224 x 2816 picture: seven 4K-layout planes of 14,942,208 bytes, the eighth out of the pool, and the HD layout's plane enlarged
status: built from the firmware's file and run in the ZV-E1's own allocator; NEVER RUN ON A CAMERA. The same ten words with 14,745,600 ran on an FX6 (dmm7slot_fx6_v1)
credit: the memory model, the seven-plane idea and the ten words: github.com/ArcaneLantern/fx6-open-gate-test issue 2 (Mininoob)
table: unit records 0x257b07c .. 0x2580b6c (parse_dmmcfg.RAM zve1_202): record = base + seq x 0x14, {0, type, key, size, attributes}
why: the ZV-E1 fills an output plane at 1.25 bytes per pixel: 13,271,040 bytes hold 3840 x 2560 (12,288,000); 4224 x 2816 needs 14,868,480
